compute.reported_as: Table I column "Triangular 48": computer Sekirei; point group D6; No. of symmetries 1152; dimension 2.8e10; No. of cores 3456; total memory 2.5 TB; memory lookup 151 MB; Time / MVM 399 s; % comm. time 39%; g.s. sector Gamma.A1.even; g.s. energy -26.8129452715. || TABLE I: Benchmark results for various problems on three different supercomputer systems described in the main text. The employed symmetries include translational, point group and spinflip symmetry. We show the total memory used by all MPI processes and the memory used by the lookup tables for the sublattice coding technique. We also show the amount of time spent for communication. || The benchmarks were performed on three different supercomputers. The Vienna Scientific Cluster VSC3 is built up from over 2020 nodes with two Intel Xeon E5-2650v2, 2.6 GHz, 8 core processors, the supercomputer Hydra at the Max Planck Supercomputing & Data Facility in Garching with over 3500 nodes with 20 core Intel Ivy Bridge 2.8 GHz processors and the System B Sekirei at the Institute for Solid State Physics of the University of Tokyo with over 1584 nodes with two Intel Xeon E5-2680v3 12 core 2.5GHz processors. Both the Hydra and Sekirei use InfiniBand FDR interconnect, whereas the VSC3 uses Intel TrueScale Infiniband for network communication.
